Listen to this article Share Liverpool came from two goals down to beat Villarreal 4-3 at Anfield on Tuesday night, with teenage winger Rio Ngumoha inspiring the comeback to maintain the Reds’ perfect start to their UEFA Champions League campaign. Villarreal raced into a two-goal lead through Georges Mikautadze and Sergi Cardona, punishing a sloppy start from Liverpool. However, Alexis Mac Allister pulled one back before half-time, and Ronald Araújo equalised on the stroke of the interval. Read Also: Champions League: Foden nets hat-trick as Man City crush AEK Athens Ngumoha then turned provider again after the break, setting up Mac Allister to put Liverpool ahead for the first time before Florian Wirtz extended their advantage with his first club goal of the season. Tani Oluwaseyi reduced the deficit late in the game, setting up a tense finish, but Liverpool held on to secure a dramatic victory. The result extended Liverpool’s winning run in Europe, although they were forced to work hard for the win. Liverpool’s defensive frailties were exposed early when Renato Veiga played a long ball that Virgil van Dijk should have dealt with. The Liverpool captain’s weak header back towards goalkeeper Alisson Becker was intercepted by Mikautadze, who finished with his left foot to put Villarreal ahead. Liverpool survived the late pressure to complete an impressive comeback, with Ngumoha emerging as the standout performer after his two decisive assists helped transform the contest. The victory underlined Liverpool’s attacking resilience,but also highlighted defensive issues that Andoni Iraola will have to fix as the Reds continues its Champions League campaign.
